subject: Request: SLA adjustment for customer-managed firewall & KMS latency attribution
messages:
From: Tom Li <tom.li@cortecsys.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Katherine Roe <katherine.roe@cortecsys.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Increased tail latency since last week - wondering about SLA carveouts

Diego,

We started to see increased tail latency on our private deployment starting late last week — 99th percentile token latencies jumping by ~180-220ms intermittently. The pattern correlates with maintenance windows on our side (we have stateful firewall updates and key rotation to our KMS HSM cluster).

Two questions:
1) From Redwood's point of view, how much of that latency would be attributed to "Customer-controlled infrastructure" versus Redwood runtime?
2) If we need a temporary SLA/latency exception while we stabilize firewall config + KMS rotation, what's the process and what language do you need for a shared-responsibility appendix?

I can share packet captures and our KMS timing logs — attaching a sample pcap and a short CSV in follow-up. We prefer not to pause rotations for compliance reasons so an exception window would be helpful.

Thanks,
Tom Li
Head of Platform Engineering
CortecSys

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodai.com>
To: Tom Li <tom.li@cortecsys.com>
Cc: Katherine Roe <katherine.roe@cortecsys.com>
Date: 2027-03-28T10:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increased tail latency since last week - wondering about SLA carveouts

Tom — thanks for the quick note and for flagging the traces you plan to share. Short answers up front:

- Attribution: Network changes (firewall stateful updates, MTU changes, proxy/NAT timeouts) and remote KMS HSM key-wrap latency are normally considered customer-controlled dependencies when they live in your VPC or on-prem stack. We generally carve those out from Redwood uptime/latency SLOs when the traffic path or crypto ops are initiated/managed by the customer.

- Process: We can put a temporary latency exception in place (30 / 60 / custom days) with a few conditions:
  * Mutually agreed observability hooks (we need prefix traces, request IDs, and KMS timing samples).
  * A mutual action plan (MAP) with target remediation milestones.
  * A clause in the shared-responsibility appendix that lists exact dependency boundaries.

Can you send the pcap and KMS timing CSV? Once we have those we’ll run an initial attribution check and propose exception language. I’ve looped in Monica (Customer Success) and Vivek (Sales/PM) so we can coordinate the MAP and contract appendix.

Best,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Tom Li <tom.li@cortecsys.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodai.com>
Cc: Katherine Roe <katherine.roe@cortecsys.com>
Date: 2027-03-29T15:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Increased tail latency since last week - wondering about SLA carveouts

Diego / team — attaching the packet capture and a short CSV with KMS call timestamps and wrap durations. Notes:
- The packet capture shows spikes that line up with our firewall rule refresh (every 6 hours) and a few NAT connection tears.
- KMS CSV has highlighted rows where wrap_time exceeds 120ms. We rotate keys nightly and the HSM cluster sometimes rebalances during that window.

Attachments: network-trace-20270328.pcap, kms-wrap-sample-20270328.csv

We'd like a 45-day exception while we implement sticky connections and adjust our firewall refresh cadence. Goal is to avoid pausing rotation. Happy to get on a call to walk through traces.

Thanks,
Tom

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwoodai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwoodai.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwoodai.com>
Date: 2027-03-30T16:05:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Increased tail latency — proposed exception language & MAP

Team — forwarding Tom's traces. Quick plan I propose:
1) Acceptance criteria (48-72 hours): Redwood will run attribution analysis within 48 hours of receiving full traces and produce a short findings note (root-cause: network vs KMS vs runtime).
2) Temporary exception: Offer a 45-day latency exception window for 99th percentile token latency where Redwood will not apply SLA credits for incidents demonstrably caused by customer-managed firewall refreshes or KMS HSM key-wrap delays as evidenced by mutually-agreed traces.
3) Observability requirements (precondition to exception): Customer must provide request_id prefixes for a sample of production requests, pcap slices, and KMS timing logs. Redwood will add an observability tag to accepted requests to simplify cross-correlation.
4) MAP milestones: Day 7 — deploy sticky connections + NAT keepalive; Day 21 — stabilize firewall refresh cadence; Day 45 — re-evaluation and formal close or extension.
5) Contract appendix (draft excerpt below to put in the exception addendum):

--- BEGIN DRAFT CLAUSE ---
Customer-Managed Dependency Carveout

For the duration of the Exception Period, Redwood's uptime and latency SLAs shall not apply to latency measured on requests for which Redwood's attribution analysis concludes that increased latency is primarily caused by Customer-Managed Dependencies. Customer-Managed Dependencies include, but are not limited to: (i) stateful firewall updates, NAT connection churn, or other network-layer modifications occurring within Customer-controlled VPCs or on-prem networks; and (ii) remote key wrap/unwrap operations performed by Customer-controlled KMS/HSM endpoints where the end-to-end cryptographic operation contributes materially to request latency.

The Exception Period is contingent upon Customer providing the observability artifacts listed in the Mutual Action Plan and cooperating with Redwood engineers during root-cause analysis. Redwood will document findings and lift the exception when remediation milestones are met.
--- END DRAFT CLAUSE ---

Monica — can you take point on the official MAP doc and add the artifacts checklist? Vivek — can you confirm we’re fine with a 45-day exception with the clause above and draft the addendum language for legal review? I’ll put together the initial findings once the pcap/CSV are ingested.

Diego
